title: WIP of my life sim game
author: rekansebangku
selftext:
Hi everyone, I'd like to share my life sim game called HariHari. This is my first attempt at building a life sim game, and I wanted to share my progress so far.

All the assets were created by myself except for the NPC avatars. The UI hasn't been touched yet, but the mechanics are coming together little by little.

This video shows how NPCs can talk and respond to you, but there's also a classic mode where all the dialogue is authored for players who don't want to use their own key for the live NPC mode. I would love to hear your thoughts on it. Thanks!

comments.author: shadowlands-mage
comments.body: Nice.  What engine you use? Godot?

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thank you! I use Godot for this game

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thank you!

comments.author: Robiety101
comments.body: Even when typing you might want them to be able to autofill items/prices so it doesn't get tedious.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Agree. That’s why I’m keeping the AI conversation layer separate from the actual transaction system. Players can use natural language if they want the roleplay experience, but there’s also a deterministic quick buy/sell UI for faster shopping.

comments.author: BendMyWang
comments.body: Nice! Can’t wait to see more!

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thank you so much! This really means a lot to me.

comments.author: KhaosPT
comments.body: Looks good my dude,  did you do the 3d graphics by yourself? Im using 2d pixel on for but I actually can't find much pixel resources anywhere. I mean there are loads, but not single collections with lots of combos.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body:
Thanks dude! Yep, I made all the 3D assets and animations myself. Since I'm a 3D artist, making assets is actually a fun break from my regular work.   
  
I don't know much about 2D sprites either, especially pixel art. I did try making 1 or 2 for a prototype, but keeping the visual style consistent is a nightmare. I figured it's best to stick with my strengths, which is 3D modeling in Blender.

replies.author: reverendblueball
replies.body:
Yeah, I can tell who has an eye for design(and sometimes code), and who is just trying to one-shot prompt the game with reckless abandon.

You're proof that this tech only augments human talent. This looks really nice. Keep going.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Man, I really appreciate you saying that. It honestly means the world to me. I’m still learning a lot along the way, but I do try my best to make sure everything has a cohesive look and feel rather than just relying completely on the tools. Hearing this kind of feedback makes all the long hours in Blender totally worth it. Thank you so much for the support!

replies.author: KhaosPT
replies.body: That explains! It looks amazing, keep it up

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thank you so much for the kind words and support! It means a lot. 🙌

comments.author: Final_Fantasy_VII
comments.body: Wow I really love the aesthetics it’s looking good

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body:
Thank you so much! I'm glad you like it. 😄  
I'm definitely channeling a lot of Harvest Moon and PS2-era nostalgia here. It's going to be a long journey since I'm making all the assets by myself, but I'm having a blast with it so far.

replies.author: Final_Fantasy_VII
replies.body: It actually reminded me of final fantasy 7 chibis if it was updated with better visuals for modern day. I really like that game and even for a remakes wanted it done isometric or like the original but with new visual like this. It looks great keep it up !

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Well, your username definitely explains it! 😄 I love FF7 too. I played it a ton as a child on my PS1, and honestly, even until now, I’ve been afraid to try the remake version because I don't want to ruin those nostalgic memories lol. Anyway, thank you so much! I really appreciate the kind words.

comments.author: OkResponsibility9182
comments.body: Why do we need to be able to talk to NPCs freely?

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Personally, I think being able to actually talk to NPCs makes the game much more immersive and personal. I get that AI features can be risky or aren't for everyone, but that's exactly why it's just a nice to have little option. Players who don't like it or aren't tech savvy can easily turn it off and play in classic mode, and it's set to classic mode by default anyway! 😄

replies.author: TopTippityTop
replies.body:
I think it would be cool if it affects things somehow.

For example, the way you talk to someone affects how they will talk to you later, what gossip (context) is shared among npcs over time, affecting your reputation

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body:
Oh man, you are going to love this because I’ve actually already implemented all of those features into the game! 😄

The way you treat NPCs will definitely impact how they react to you later on, and the gossip system is already running behind the scenes to dynamically shape your reputation. Hearing that this is exactly what you're looking for makes me so happy and confirms I'm on the right track.   
  
Thank you so much for the awesome feedback!

replies.author: OkResponsibility9182
replies.body: I get it, I was just curious about the reason. You should try switching to google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, turn off thinking, and enable streaming. It'll make the AI respond much faster.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Oh, wow, I didn't know about that! Thanks for the tip, that's actually super helpful for the game. I’ll definitely give it a shot!

comments.author: HobiAI
comments.body: Mbak Kasir HariHari Swalayan : The Game 😄

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: wkwkwk, coming soon 😉

comments.author: d-czar
comments.body:
This looks fantastic— one of the nicest looking games I’ve seen in this sub.  Are you using mcp in Godot? If not, give Godot AI a try.  We’re closing in on 1000 GitHub stars and an active development community.  Love to hear if it helps you.  Totally free and open source. 

https://store.godotengine.org/asset/dlight/godot-ai/

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thanks! Yep, I'm currently using the Godot MCP tool from the asset library, and I occasionally mess around with GodotIQ too. Will definitely give Godot AI a look!

comments.author: coyote1942
comments.body:
Looks really good. Really glad you did the classic mode. Every developer seems to choose the option forcing players to come up with dialog and type or speak it out.  One cool mechanic I think would be interesting  is based on your mood and or status you would have a specific dialog lines generated to say.   
Like if you are hungry you might have a grouchy line.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body:
Thank you! Yeah, I don't like being forced into mechanics that I don't feel are necessary, so I just made it a nice-to-have feature. 😄

Ooh, actually, that's a great idea! I think I'll definitely implement that in the future. Thank you for the insight and the kind words!

comments.author: astanar
comments.body: Awesome! What did you use to make the art?

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thank you! I use Blender for the 3d assets and animation

comments.author: Extra-Yard-7458
comments.body: The 2d art and the UI looks too AI which is extremely unattractive, other than that looks good

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: ​Fair enough! I completely agree, and those two areas are definitely on my list to learn and change later. That’s pretty much why I noted that the avatar and UI are still completely untouched for now. Thanks a lot for the feedback, I appreciate you pointing it out!

comments.author: FeelingCareful3358
comments.body: Lovely environment, but I’m concerned with the use of derogatory names, the bread seller called you Dik (as in Dick), why? I know she’s only one star relationship with you, so not very pleasant, but calling you a Dik?

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body:
Thank you so much! I'm really glad you like the environment.

Aaand as for your concern, I love that you noticed that detail, but it’s actually not what it looks like! Since the game is set in Indonesia (forgot to mention that in the post, my bad), "Dik" is a polite and respectful term here (short for "Adik," which means younger sibling). Elders or shopkeepers use it to kindly address someone who looks younger than them. She’s being friendly, I promise! Thanks for watching so closely!

replies.author: FeelingCareful3358
replies.body: Koop, never knew that. TBH I was known as Mr Dicktionary on Eve Online for correcting everyone else’s spelling. It’s mad, I see typo’s everywhere, it’s like I can’t unsee it, so when dik popped up, I had to rewind the video 😂😁

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Haha, that makes perfect sense now! That’s actually a hilarious backstory. 😂 I guess "dik" was the ultimate boss fight for Mr Dicktionary! Thanks for the laughs, man, and I'm glad we got that cleared up!

comments.author: Background-Bear7441
comments.body: Looks cozy, I'm also interested in building life sim game. But then I realized the scope is too big for one person and it could take many years to finish.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body:
Thanks! I completely get what you mean, To be honest, I get overwhelmed by the scope sometimes too.

What really helps me is breaking the roadmap into bite-sized features. If a big system drives me crazy, I'll work on a small mechanic or model a few simple 3D assets just to refresh and hit a quick milestone. It's a marathon, but totally doable if you break it down!

replies.author: Background-Bear7441
replies.body: sound good, looking forward for more preview of the game👍

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thank you!

comments.author: Substantial-Cat2598
comments.body: This is interesting, have you thought about also ask AI to generate chat options to pick from instead of typing? I just imagine myself type there and probably will feel tired. :P

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body:
Wow, I love this suggestion!

Having the AI generate a few preset choice options to click on is a great way to keep things chill and accessible. It’s definitely doable, and I’ll absolutely look into implementing this. Thanks for the brilliant idea!

replies.author: Substantial-Cat2598
replies.body: Glad it helped, btw, this is really cool project, can’t wait to see more NPCs roaming around.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thank you so much! That really motivates me to keep pushing forward. I'm currently working on bringing more life to the village, so there will definitely be more NPCs roaming around soon. Stay tuned! 🙌

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Haha, thank you so much! It really means a lot that you want to play it. The game is still cooking, but I'll definitely do a playtest or release a demo once it’s ready. Stay tuned! 🚀

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thank you!

comments.author: forever_____young
comments.body: It's already been released, what's the name, and will it be available for Android?

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: It's still under development and will release targeting this year on PC
